Primitive elements and number fields

Source: R/polys-algebraic-number.R, R/polys-options.R
primitive_element.Rd

primitive_element(extension, x) finds a primitive element of the field generated by the algebraic numbers in extension, as SymPy's primitive_element(): it returns its minimal polynomial and the integer coefficients c with theta = sum(c * extension); with ex = TRUE also the coordinates of each extension in the power basis of theta (highest power first). to_number_field(extension, theta) expresses the primitive element of extension in the field of theta as an AlgebraicNumber(), and field_isomorphism(a, b) returns the coordinates of a in the power basis of b (highest power first), or NULL when a is not in Q(b).

Usage

field_isomorphism(a, b)

to_number_field(extension, theta = NULL, gen = NULL, alias = NULL)

primitive_element(extension, x = NULL, ex = FALSE)

Arguments

a, b

Algebraic numbers.

extension

An algebraic number or a list of them.

theta

A generator of the target field.

gen

The variable of the minimal polynomial of the result.

alias

A symbol (or name) printed for the generator.

x

The variable of the minimal polynomial (a dummy by default).

ex

Also return the coordinates of the extensions.

Value

A list, an AlgebraicNumber, or NULL.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x")
primitive_element(list(sqrt(Integer(2)), sqrt(Integer(3))), x)
#> [[1]]
#> x^4 - 10*x^2 + 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> 1
#> 
#> 
field_isomorphism(sqrt(Integer(2)), sqrt(Integer(2)) + sqrt(Integer(3)))
#> [[1]]
#> 1/2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 0
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> -9/2
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> 0
#> 
to_number_field(sqrt(Integer(2)), sqrt(Integer(2)) + sqrt(Integer(3)))
#> sqrt(2)
